items.prompt:
Function `Replace()` will:

1. take three parameters: a string (the original string), a char (the original character) and a char (the new character)
2. form a new string from the original string in which all instances of the original character are replaced by the new character
3. return the new string.

Write pseudocode for function `Replace()`.

criteria.point: Function heading and ending, including the three parameters and the STRING return type
Declaration of the local variables used, including the loop counter
Loop that runs for the length of the original string
Extracts each character and tests it against the original character, inside the loop
Uses concatenation to build the new string, replacing the character where necessary, inside the loop
Returns the new string after a reasonable attempt

rejects: Marking points 4 and 5 must be inside the loop
Return of NewString is awarded after a reasonable attempt
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION Replace(OldString : STRING, Char1, Char2 : CHAR) RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE NewString : STRING
   DECLARE ThisChar : CHAR
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER

   NewString ← ""
   FOR Index ← 1 TO LENGTH(OldString)
      ThisChar ← MID(OldString, Index, 1)
      IF ThisChar = Char1 THEN
         ThisChar ← Char2
      ENDIF
      NewString ← NewString & ThisChar
   NEXT Index

   RETURN NewString
ENDFUNCTION

items.prompt:
A video-conferencing program supports up to six users. Speech from each user is sampled and digitised, and the digitised values are stored in the 2D integer array `Sample`, which has 6 rows by 128 columns. Each row holds the 128 sound samples from one user.

The samples are processed into a single value per column, stored in the 1D integer array `Result`. This is done by procedure `Mix()`, which will:

- calculate the average of each of the 6 sound samples in a column
- ignore sound sample values of 10 or less
- store the average value in the corresponding position in `Result`
- repeat for each column in `Sample`

Example values from the diagram (rows are users 1-6, columns shown are 1, 2, 3, ..., 126, 127, 128):

| Row \ Column | 1 | 2 | 3 | ... | 126 | 127 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 20 | 20 | 20 | ... | 30 | 30 | 2 |
| 2 | 20 | 20 | 30 | ... | 50 | 30 | 3 |
| 3 | 20 | 20 | 40 | ... | 40 | 40 | 4 |
| 4 | 20 | 20 | 50 | ... | 40 | 50 | 20 |
| 5 | 20 | 3 | 5 | ... | 6 | 60 | 4 |
| 6 | 20 | 4 | 2 | ... | 4 | 70 | 30 |
| **Result** | 20 | 20 | 35 | ... | 40 | 46 | 25 |

Write pseudocode for procedure `Mix()`. Assume `Sample` and `Result` are global.
items.context_note: Sample is a global 6 x 128 INTEGER 2D array; Result is a global 1D INTEGER array of 128 elements.

criteria.point: Declares and initialises Count and Total before the inner loop (reset for each column)
Outer loop for 128 iterations (each column)
Inner loop for 6 iterations (each user/row)
Tests whether the sample is greater than 10, inside the loop
If true, adds the sample to Total and increments Count
Calculates the average and assigns it to the Result element after the inner loop and within the outer loop
Uses INT() or DIV to convert the average to an integer

rejects: Scheme: Max 6 marks (seven marking points)

The scheme's model declares 'Count, Total ThisNum' (a typo in the printed scheme); the model above corrects it to 'Count, Total'. The model does not guard against Count = 0, which the scheme does not penalise
items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE Mix()
   DECLARE Count, Total : INTEGER
   DECLARE ThisUser, ThisSample : INTEGER

   FOR ThisSample ← 1 TO 128
      Count ← 0
      Total ← 0
      FOR ThisUser ← 1 TO 6
         IF Sample[ThisUser, ThisSample] > 10 THEN
            Count ← Count + 1
            Total ← Total + Sample[ThisUser, ThisSample]
         ENDIF
      NEXT ThisUser
      Result[ThisSample] ← INT(Total / Count)
   NEXT ThisSample
ENDPROCEDURE

items.prompt:
A computer shop assembles computers using items bought from several suppliers. A text file Stock.txt contains information about each item. Information for each item is one line in Stock.txt in the format:

`<ItemNum><SupplierCode><Description>`

| Field | Format | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| ItemNum | 4 numeric characters | unique for each item, in the range "0001" to "5999" inclusive |
| SupplierCode | 5 alphabetic characters | identifies the supplier of the item |
| Description | a string | a minimum of 12 characters |

The file is organised in ascending order of ItemNum and does not contain all possible values in the range.

A programmer has started to define program modules:

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| SuppExists() (already written) | called with a string parameter representing a supplier code; returns TRUE if the supplier code is already in use, otherwise FALSE |
| IsNewSupp() | called with a string parameter representing a new supplier code; returns TRUE if the string only contains alphabetic characters (upper or lower case) and the supplier code is not already in use, otherwise returns FALSE |

Write pseudocode for module `IsNewSupp()`. Module `SuppExists()` has already been written and should be used as part of your solution. `SuppExists()` will generate a run-time error if the given parameter is not 5 characters in length.
items.context_note: SuppExists(Code : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN already exists; it runs into a run-time error if Code is not exactly 5 characters.

criteria.point: Checks that ThisString is exactly 5 characters in length
Uses SuppExists() with a 5-character string as the parameter (only called after the length check)
Loop for 5 iterations / for the length of the string parameter
Extracts a character inside the loop
Tests whether the character is alphabetic, inside the loop
...catering for both upper and lower case
Returns a Boolean following a reasonable attempt

rejects: SuppExists() must only be called with a 5-character string, so the length check must come first
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION IsNewSupp(ThisString : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER
   DECLARE ThisChar : CHAR

   IF LENGTH(ThisString) <> 5 THEN
      RETURN FALSE      // invalid SupplierCode length
   ENDIF

   IF SuppExists(ThisString) THEN
      RETURN FALSE      // SupplierCode already exists
   ENDIF

   FOR Index ← 1 TO 5
      ThisChar ← TO_LOWER(MID(ThisString, Index, 1))
      IF ThisChar < 'a' OR ThisChar > 'z' THEN
         RETURN FALSE
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index

   RETURN TRUE
ENDFUNCTION

items.prompt:
A computer shop assembles computers using items bought from several suppliers. A text file Stock.txt contains information about each item. Information for each item is one line in Stock.txt in the format:

`<ItemNum><SupplierCode><Description>`

| Field | Format | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| ItemNum | 4 numeric characters | unique for each item, in the range "0001" to "5999" inclusive |
| SupplierCode | 5 alphabetic characters | identifies the supplier of the item |
| Description | a string | a minimum of 12 characters |

The file is organised in ascending order of ItemNum and does not contain all possible values in the range.

A new module is defined:

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| CheckNewItem() | called with a string parameter representing a line of item information; checks whether an item with the same ItemNum already exists in the file; returns TRUE if the ItemNum is not already in the file, otherwise returns FALSE |

Write efficient pseudocode for module `CheckNewItem()`.
items.context_note: The file is in ascending order of ItemNum, so an efficient solution stops early once ItemNum passes the one being searched for.

criteria.point: Opens Stock.txt in READ mode and subsequently closes it
Extracts NewItemNum (first 4 characters) from the parameter
Conditional loop that runs until EOF("Stock.txt")
...OR until the NewItemNum is found
...OR until ThisItemNum is no longer less than NewItemNum (efficient early stop using the ascending order)
Reads a line from Stock.txt AND extracts ThisItemNum, inside the loop
If ThisItemNum = NewItemNum then terminates the loop / sets a flag, inside the loop
Returns a Boolean after a reasonable attempt

items.max_note: 8 points available, max 7; max 6 if the function wrapper (heading and ending) is missing or incorrect
rejects: Scheme: Max 7 marks
Max 6 if the function heading/ending is missing or incorrect
Brackets around the READFILE arguments are optional
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION CheckNewItem(NewLine : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE NotFound : BOOLEAN
   DECLARE NewItemNum, ThisItemNum, ThisLine : STRING

   NotFound ← TRUE

   OPENFILE "Stock.txt" FOR READ
   NewItemNum ← LEFT(NewLine, 4)
   ThisItemNum ← "0000"    // rogue initial value

   WHILE NOT EOF("Stock.txt") AND NotFound = TRUE AND ThisItemNum < NewItemNum
      READFILE("Stock.txt", ThisLine)    // brackets optional
      ThisItemNum ← LEFT(ThisLine, 4)
      IF ThisItemNum = NewItemNum THEN
         NotFound ← FALSE
      ENDIF
   ENDWHILE

   CLOSEFILE "Stock.txt"

   RETURN NotFound
ENDFUNCTION

A function GetNum() takes two parameters, a string and a character, counts how many times the character occurs in the string, and returns the count. Character comparison is case sensitive ('a' and 'A' are different).

Write pseudocode for function GetNum().

criteria.point: Function heading and ending, including both parameters and the INTEGER return type
Declares local INTEGER variables for the loop index and the count
Loop for the length of the string parameter
Extracts a character and compares it (case sensitive, no case conversion) with the character parameter, inside the loop
Increments Count on a match, inside the loop
Returns Count after the loop

rejects: Comparison must be case sensitive; do not convert case
items.final_answer:
Function GetNum(ThisString : STRING, ThisChar : CHAR) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Index, Count : INTEGER

   Count ← 0

   FOR Index ← 1 TO LENGTH(ThisString)
      IF MID(ThisString, Index, 1) = ThisChar THEN
         Count ← Count + 1
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index
   RETURN Count

ENDFUNCTION

A procedure Square() takes an integer in the range 1 to 9 as a parameter and outputs a number square. The boundary is made up of the digit for the parameter value; the inside is made up of asterisks (*).

Examples of output:

```
Parameter 1:   Parameter 2:   Parameter 3:   Parameter 4:   ... Parameter 9:
1              22             333            4444               999999999
               22             3*3            4**4               9*******9
                              333            4**4               9*******9
                                             4444               9*******9
                                                                9*******9
                                                                9*******9
                                                                9*******9
                                                                9*******9
                                                                999999999
```

Each pseudocode OUTPUT statement starts its output on a new line, e.g. OUTPUT "Hello" / OUTPUT "ginger" / OUTPUT "cat" displays three lines.

Write pseudocode for procedure Square(). Parameter validation is not required.

criteria.point: Procedure heading and ending including the integer parameter
Loop using the parameter, containing an attempt to construct the first/last line
Correctly constructs the first/last line (the digit repeated Dim times)
Attempt at a loop to construct the intermediate line (digit, Dim-2 asterisks, digit)
Outputs the first/last line of the square when Dim > 2
Outputs all intermediate lines in a loop
Correct output of the first two squares (parameter 1 gives one line '1'; parameter 2 gives two lines '22')

items.max_note: max 6 (the scheme lists 7 points for loop-based solutions)
rejects: Selection-based (CASE) solutions are marked on a separate 6-point scheme: heading and ending including parameter; correct use of parameter to select all required squares; correct output of first two squares; at least six squares correctly output; at least one loop to output lines with multiple asterisks; all number squares output correctly
Note: one-digit square: the single digit '1' must be output as a single line only (hence the IF Dim <> 1 test)
items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE Square(Dim : INTEGER)
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER
   DECLARE ThisChar : CHAR
   DECLARE StringA, StringB : STRING
   CONSTANT FILLER = '*'

   StringA ← ""

   ThisChar ← NUM_TO_STR(Dim)

   FOR Count ← 1 TO Dim
      StringA ← StringA & ThisChar    // build up first & last line
   NEXT Count

   StringB ← ThisChar
   FOR Count ← 1 TO Dim - 2
      StringB ← StringB & FILLER      // build up intermediate line
   NEXT Count
   StringB ← StringB & ThisChar       // add final digit

   OUTPUT StringA
   FOR Count ← 1 TO Dim - 2
      OUTPUT StringB
   NEXT Count

   IF Dim <> 1 THEN
      OUTPUT StringA
   ENDIF

ENDPROCEDURE

// Selection-based alternative (also accepted): CASE OF Dim with one branch per value 1 to 9, each outputting the whole square (e.g. 4 : OUTPUT "4444" / FOR Count ← 1 TO 2 / OUTPUT "4**4" / NEXT Count / OUTPUT "4444").

A computer shop assembles computers from items bought from several suppliers. A text file Stock.txt holds one line per item in the format <ItemNum><SupplierCode><Description>, with no separators.

| Field | Format | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| ItemNum | 4 numeric characters | unique number for each item in the range "0001" to "5999" inclusive |
| SupplierCode | 3 alphabetic characters | identifies the supplier of the item |
| Description | a string | a minimum of 12 characters |

The file is in ascending order of ItemNum and does not contain all possible values in the range.

Modules:
- OnlyAlpha() (already written): takes a string, returns TRUE if it contains only alphabetic characters, otherwise FALSE.
- CheckInfo(): takes a string representing a line of item information, returns TRUE if the item information is valid, otherwise FALSE.

Write pseudocode for module CheckInfo(). Module OnlyAlpha() should be used as part of your solution.

criteria.point: Tests the length of the parameter (minimum 4 + 3 + 12 = 19 characters)
Extracts the first 4 characters of the parameter as the ItemNum
Tests that all four of those characters are numeric (e.g. IS_NUM on each character)
Tests ItemNum is in the range "0001" to "5999"
Extracts characters 5 to 7 of the parameter as the SupplierCode
Uses OnlyAlpha() with the extracted SupplierCode
Returns a BOOLEAN value correctly in all cases (must be declared as local)

rejects: Return of BOOLEAN value only earns the mark if the variable has been declared as local (the model uses direct RETURN statements)
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION CheckInfo(NewLine : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE ThisNum : STRING
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER

   IF LENGTH(NewLine) < 19 THEN
      RETURN FALSE
   ENDIF

   FOR Index ← 1 TO 4
      IF NOT IS_NUM(MID(NewLine, Index, 1)) THEN
         RETURN FALSE
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index

   ThisNum ← LEFT(NewLine, 4)

   IF ThisNum < "0001" OR ThisNum > "5999" THEN
      RETURN FALSE
   ENDIF

   IF NOT OnlyAlpha(MID(NewLine, 5, 3)) THEN
      RETURN FALSE
   ENDIF

   RETURN TRUE

ENDFUNCTION

Modules:

- CheckInfo(): takes a string representing a line of item information, returns TRUE if the item information is valid, otherwise FALSE.

A new module AddItem() is defined: it takes a string holding valid information for a new item that is not currently in Stock.txt, creates a new file NewStock.txt from the contents of Stock.txt, and adds the new item information at the appropriate place in NewStock.txt. (Stock.txt is in ascending order of ItemNum and does not contain all values in the range.)

Write pseudocode for module AddItem().

criteria.point: Opens both files in the correct modes (Stock.txt READ, NewStock.txt WRITE) and closes them afterwards
Conditional loop until the end of file Stock.txt
Reads a line from Stock.txt and extracts ThisItemNum, inside the loop
Tests ThisItemNum > NewItemNum then writes NewLine to NewStock.txt (inside the loop)
...including a mechanism to do this once only
Writes the line read from Stock.txt to NewStock.txt
Deals with the case where NewLine is the new last line of the file

rejects: Array-based solution is marked on: open both files in correct modes and close; declare AND initialise Temp array; store NewLine in appropriate array element; loop until end of file Stock.txt; read a line AND extract Index in the loop; assign line read to appropriate array element in the loop; loop through array writing non-blank elements to NewStock.txt
items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE AddItem(NewLine : STRING)
   DECLARE NewItemNum, ThisItemNum, ThisLine : STRING

   OPENFILE "Stock.txt" FOR READ
   OPENFILE "NewStock.txt" FOR WRITE
   NewItemNum ← LEFT(NewLine, 4)

   WHILE NOT EOF("Stock.txt")
      READFILE("Stock.txt", ThisLine)
      ThisItemNum ← LEFT(ThisLine, 4)
      IF ThisItemNum > NewItemNum THEN
         WRITEFILE("NewStock.txt", NewLine)   // write NewLine...
         NewItemNum ← "9999"                  // ...once only
      ENDIF
      WRITEFILE("NewStock.txt", ThisLine)
   ENDWHILE

   IF NewItemNum <> "9999" THEN
      WRITEFILE("NewStock.txt", NewLine)      // new last line in the file
   ENDIF

   CLOSEFILE "Stock.txt"
   CLOSEFILE "NewStock.txt"
ENDPROCEDURE

// Array-based alternative (also accepted): declare and initialise Temp : ARRAY[1:5999] OF STRING to ""; store NewLine in Temp[STR_TO_NUM(LEFT(NewLine, 4))]; read each line of Stock.txt into Temp at the index given by its first 4 characters; then loop through Temp writing the non-blank elements to NewStock.txt.

A function MakeString() will:

1. take two parameters: a count (integer) and a character
2. build a string whose length equals the count, made up entirely of that character
3. return the string, or return "ERROR" if the count is less than 1.

FUNCTION MakeString(Count : INTEGER, AChar : CHAR) RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE MyString : STRING
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER

   IF Count < 1 THEN
      MyString <- "ERROR"
   ELSE
      MyString <- ""
      FOR Index <- 1 TO Count
         MyString <- MyString & AChar
      NEXT Index
   ENDIF

   RETURN MyString
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION ChangeSupp(Code1, Code2 : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER
   DECLARE ThisLine, ThisCode : STRING

   OPENFILE "Stock.txt" FOR READ
   OPENFILE "NewStock.txt" FOR WRITE
   Count <- 0
   WHILE NOT EOF("Stock.txt")
      READFILE("Stock.txt", ThisLine)
      ThisCode <- MID(ThisLine, 5, 3)
      IF ThisCode = Code1 THEN
         ThisLine <- LEFT(ThisLine, 4) & Code2 & RIGHT(ThisLine, LENGTH(ThisLine) - 7)
         Count <- Count + 1
      ENDIF
      WRITEFILE("NewStock.txt", ThisLine)
   ENDWHILE

   CLOSEFILE "NewStock.txt"
   CLOSEFILE "Stock.txt"

   RETURN Count
ENDFUNCTION

DestinationID and SourceID are three numeric characters each, and Data is a variable-length string of at least 1 character. items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE SendFile(FileName, DestID : STRING, Port : INTEGER)
   DECLARE FileData : STRING
   CONSTANT STX = CHR(02)
   CONSTANT ETX = CHR(03)
   OPENFILE FileName FOR READ
   WHILE NOT EOF(FileName)

      FileData ← STX & DestID & MyID & FileData & ETX
      CALL Transmit(FileData, Port)

   CLOSEFILE FileName

ENDPROCEDURE

```

```

Columns 1 and 2 of each row define a range of ID values (lowest and highest) and column 3 gives the port to use for a destination in that range. Unused rows have column 1 set to -1 (the other two columns are undefined and can be anywhere). Example contents:

| | Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Row 1 | 100 | 199 | 1 |
| Row 2 | 200 | 259 | 2 |
| Row 3 | -1 | undefined | undefined |
| Row 4 | 260 | 399 | 2 |
| Row 5 | 400 | 599 | 3 |
| Row 6 | 600 | 999 | 1 |

Each computer has a unique three-digit ID and three serial ports (each identified by an integer). Messages are strings of the form <DestinationID><Data>. criteria.point: Function heading and ending with the string parameter and RETURNS INTEGER
Converts the string parameter to a number (STR_TO_NUM)
Loop through the rows of RouteTable (conditional loop, or a FOR over rows 1 to 6)
Skips unused rows (column 1 = -1) inside the loop
Attempts to check one range against the destination inside the loop
Tests every range correctly: lower bound <= destination AND destination <= upper bound
Stores the port (column 3) when the destination matches (and exits the loop)
Returns the port value, including -1 if no match was found

items.max_note: max 7 from 8 points. The scheme also gives a selection-statement version (six separate IF statements, one per row) with points: heading/ending; convert parameter; skip all unused elements; attempt to check one range; check two ranges correctly; check all ranges correctly; store port if matched; return port including -1. Mark the loop or the selection version, whichever the student wrote.
rejects: The printed selection example in the scheme writes the comparisons the wrong way round (RouteTable[n,1] >= DNum AND RouteTable[n,2] <= DNum) although the marking points say the ranges must be checked correctly; the intended test is lower <= DNum <= upper
Any loop type is accepted (REPEAT, WHILE, or FOR over rows 1 to 6)
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION GetPort(ThisDest : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Index, DNum, Port : INTEGER

   DNum ← STR_TO_NUM(ThisDest)
   Index ← 1
   Port ← -1

   REPEAT
      IF RouteTable[Index, 1] <> -1 THEN
         IF DNum >= RouteTable[Index, 1] AND DNum <= RouteTable[Index, 2] THEN
            Port ← RouteTable[Index, 3]
         ENDIF
      ENDIF
      Index ← Index + 1
   UNTIL Index = 7 OR Port <> -1

   RETURN Port

ENDFUNCTION

Copies of the same program run on each computer. A global string variable MyID holds the unique ID of the computer running the program. Received messages are placed on one of two stacks: stack 1 for messages that have reached their destination and stack 2 for messages to be forwarded.

- StackMsg(message : STRING, stackNum : INTEGER) returns TRUE if the message was added to the required stack, otherwise FALSE.

Module to write:
- ProcessMsg() takes a message (string); ignores any message with a zero-length data field; extracts the DestinationID from the message (the first three characters); checks whether the DestinationID is this computer or whether the message is to be forwarded; uses StackMsg() to add the message to the appropriate stack; outputs an error if the message could not be added to the stack.

items.context_note: A class is developing a program to send data between computers on a wired network. Each computer has a unique three-digit ID and three serial ports (each identified by an integer). Messages are strings of the form <DestinationID><Data>. A global 2D array RouteTable gives the port to use to forward a message.

criteria.point: Ignores the message if the data field is empty (e.g. LENGTH(ThisMsg) >= 4)
Extracts the destination from the message (e.g. LEFT(ThisMsg, 3))
Tests whether the destination is this computer (compares with MyID)
Attempts to use StackMsg()
Fully correct use of StackMsg() for both cases: message and stack 1 when it is for this computer, message and stack 2 otherwise
Tests the StackMsg() return value for both cases
After a reasonable attempt at the return-value test, outputs a warning/error if StackMsg() returns FALSE

items.max_note: one mark per point (7 points, 7 marks)
rejects: The error output mark depends on a reasonable attempt at testing the return value (point 6)
items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE ProcessMsg(ThisMsg : STRING)
   DECLARE ThisDest : STRING
   DECLARE Response : BOOLEAN
   DECLARE StackNum : INTEGER

   IF LENGTH(ThisMsg) >= 4 THEN

      ThisDest ← LEFT(ThisMsg, 3)

      IF ThisDest = MyID THEN   // It's for this computer
         StackNum ← 1
      ELSE
         StackNum ← 2
      ENDIF

      Response ← StackMsg(ThisMsg, StackNum)

      IF Response = FALSE THEN
         OUTPUT "Message discarded - no room on stack"
      ENDIF

   ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE

FUNCTION TestNum(ThisNum : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER

Each computer runs a copy of the same program with a global string MyID holding its own three-digit ID. Computers form a wired network, each has a unique three-digit ID, three ports (each identified by an integer) and connects to one to three other computers.

criteria.point: Open the file in WRITE mode and subsequently close it
Conditional loop that repeats until the terminator "****" is received
Attempted use of GetData() (ignore CALL)
Fully correct use of GetData() to return the data inside the loop
Maintain the character count (adding LENGTH of each data field) inside the loop
Write each data item to the file inside the loop, except the terminator
Final output of the message giving the number of characters written, placed outside the loop

rejects: Ignore CALL when GetData() is used (for the 'attempted use' point).
The final output may be written OUTPUT CharCount (, " characters were written to ", FileName); the count is the essential part.
items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE ReceiveFile(FileName : STRING)
   DECLARE FileData : STRING
   DECLARE CharCount : INTEGER
   CONSTANT Terminator = "****"
   OPENFILE FileName FOR WRITE
   FileData ← GetData()
   CharCount ← 0
   WHILE FileData <> Terminator
      WRITEFILE FileName, FileData
      CharCount ← CharCount + LENGTH(FileData)
      FileData ← GetData()
   ENDWHILE
   CLOSEFILE FileName
   OUTPUT CharCount, " characters were written to ", FileName
ENDPROCEDURE

Example: data "Hello Jack" sent from computer "202" to computer "454" is `<STX>"454202Hello Jack"<ETX>`. Each computer runs a copy of the same program with a global string MyID holding its own three-digit ID. Computers form a wired network, each has a unique three-digit ID, three ports (each identified by an integer) and connects to one to three other computers.

criteria.point: Conditional loop (e.g. REPEAT ... UNTIL or WHILE)
Test for the terminator "Bye" in both cases (received data and sent data)
Use GetData() to get the data from the received message
OUTPUT the received data inside the loop
INPUT the user's reply data
Attempted use of Transmit() to send the reply inside the loop
Correct formation of the message parameter to Transmit(): STX & Destination & MyID & Data & ETX, with the port as second argument

rejects: Ignore CALL for Transmit/GetData.
items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE Chat(Destination : STRING, Port : INTEGER)
   DECLARE Data : STRING
   DECLARE Finished : BOOLEAN
   CONSTANT Terminator = "Bye"
   CONSTANT STX = CHR(2)
   CONSTANT ETX = CHR(3)
   Finished ← FALSE
   REPEAT
      Data ← GetData()
      OUTPUT Data
      IF Data = Terminator THEN
         Finished ← TRUE
      ENDIF
      IF NOT Finished THEN
         INPUT Data
         Transmit(STX & Destination & MyID & Data & ETX, Port)
         IF Data = Terminator THEN
            Finished ← TRUE
         ENDIF
      ENDIF
   UNTIL Finished = TRUE
ENDPROCEDURE

A function `Check()` will: total the element values in odd index locations (1, 3, 5 ... 97, 99); total the element values in even index locations (2, 4, 6 ... 98, 100); return one of three strings 'Odd', 'Even' or 'Same' to show which total is greater, or whether the totals are the same. criteria.point: Correct function heading, ENDFUNCTION and RETURNS STRING

items.final_answer:
FUNCTION Check() RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE Odd, Even, Index : INTEGER

   Odd <- 0
   Even <- 0

   FOR Index <- 1 TO 100
      IF Index MOD 2 = 0 THEN
         Even <- Even + Data[Index]
      ELSE
         Odd <- Odd + Data[Index]
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index

   IF Odd > Even THEN
      RETURN "Odd"
   ELSE
      IF Even > Odd THEN
         RETURN "Even"
      ELSE
         RETURN "Same"
      ENDIF
   ENDIF

ENDFUNCTION

Complete the pseudocode for the function `IsRA()`, which takes the coordinates of the three endpoints of a triangle and returns TRUE if they form a right-angled triangle, otherwise FALSE.

```

   ...
ENDFUNCTION
```
items.context_note: Three points on a grid form a triangle with side lengths A, B and C. The triangle is right-angled if A^2 = B^2 + C^2 where A is the longest side. The square of a side's length from endpoints (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is (x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2. Worked example: endpoints (3, 2) and (6, 6) give B^2 = (3-6)^2 + (2-6)^2 = 9 + 16 = 25. In pseudocode the exponent operator is `^`, e.g. `Value ^ 2`.

criteria.point: Calculate the square of the length of at least one side using the coordinate formula
Calculate all three squared lengths correctly (between points 1-2, 1-3 and 2-3)
At least one correct comparison of the squared lengths (e.g. Len1 = Len2 + Len3)
All three comparisons are made (each side taken as the longest in turn)
The three comparisons are combined with logical operators (OR) or nested IFs; completely correct selection
Return TRUE or FALSE correctly in both cases

rejects: The printed model uses line continuation after OR; any layout of the condition is fine
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION IsRA(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3 : INTEGER) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE Len1, Len2, Len3 : INTEGER

   Len1 <- (x1 - x2) ^ 2 + (y1 - y2) ^ 2
   Len2 <- (x1 - x3) ^ 2 + (y1 - y3) ^ 2
   Len3 <- (x2 - x3) ^ 2 + (y2 - y3) ^ 2

   IF (Len1 = Len2 + Len3) OR (Len2 = Len1 + Len3) OR (Len3 = Len1 + Len2) THEN
      RETURN TRUE
   ELSE
      RETURN FALSE
   ENDIF

ENDFUNCTION

items.context_note: A teacher is designing a program to process pseudocode projects written by students. Each project is stored in a text file. Files are named like MichaelAday_src.txt (student project), MichaelAday_S1.txt (stage 1 output) and MichaelAday_S2.txt (stage 2 output).

criteria.point: Loop that runs to the length of Line (or length - 1)

items.final_answer:
FUNCTION DeleteComment(Line : STRING) RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE NewLine, TwoChars : STRING
   DECLARE Count, TrimTo : INTEGER
   CONSTANT Comment = "//"

   NewLine <- Line
   TrimTo <- 0
   Count <- 1
   WHILE Count < LENGTH(Line) AND TrimTo = 0
      TwoChars <- MID(Line, Count, 2) // extract 2 chars
      IF TwoChars = Comment THEN
         TrimTo <- Count
      ENDIF
      Count <- Count + 1
   ENDWHILE

   IF TrimTo <> 0 THEN
      NewLine <- LEFT(Line, TrimTo - 1)
   ENDIF

   RETURN NewLine

ENDFUNCTION

Marks 4, 5, 6 must be inside the loop
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION Stage_1(StudentName : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER

   DECLARE OldFile, NewFile, Line : STRING
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER

   OldFile <- StudentName & "_src.txt"
   NewFile <- StudentName & "_S1.txt"
   OPENFILE OldFile FOR READ
   OPENFILE NewFile FOR WRITE
   Count <- 0

   WHILE NOT EOF(OldFile)
      READFILE OldFile, Line
      Line <- DeleteComment(Line)
      IF LENGTH(Line) <> 0 THEN
         WRITEFILE NewFile, Line
         Count <- Count + 1
      ENDIF
   ENDWHILE

   CLOSEFILE OldFile
   CLOSEFILE NewFile

   RETURN Count
ENDFUNCTION

A music player has a display showing the current track, with room for 16 characters. Track titles longer than 16 characters must be trimmed as follows:

- Three dots are added to the end of the last word displayed when one or more words have been removed.

| Original title | Display string |
|---|---|
| `Bat out of Hull` | `Bat out of Hull` |
| `Bohemian Symphony` | `Bohemian...` |
| `Paperbook Writer` | `Paperbook Writer` |
| `Chris Sings the Blues` | `Chris Sings...` |
| `Green Home Alabama` | `Green Home...` |

A function `Trim()` takes a string (the original title) and returns the string to be displayed. Assume: words are separated by a single space; there are no spaces before the first word or after the last word; the first word is less than 14 characters long.

Write pseudocode for the function `Trim()`.

criteria.point: Function heading, ending, parameter and return type (FUNCTION Trim(Name : STRING) RETURNS STRING ... ENDFUNCTION)
If the length of the original string is <= 16, returns the original string unchanged
Uses a conditional loop (e.g. WHILE / REPEAT) to shorten the title
... which continues until the string is short enough (less than 14 characters, i.e. LENGTH <= 13)
Inner conditional loop or second condition to identify the word(s) to remove from the end of the string
Attempts to strip characters back to a space (e.g. removing the last character with LEFT / LENGTH)
Correct removal of the word or words from the end, including removing the final space
Concatenates the three dots ("...") to the result and returns it

rejects: The scheme lists 8 marking points but the maximum is 7 marks.
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION Trim(Name : STRING) RETURNS STRING
   CONSTANT Dots = "..."
   CONSTANT Space = " "
   IF LENGTH(Name) <= 16 THEN
      RETURN Name
   ENDIF
   // Otherwise it has to be trimmed
   WHILE LENGTH(Name) > 13
      REPEAT
         Name ← LEFT(Name, LENGTH(Name) - 1)   // strip last char
      UNTIL RIGHT(Name, 1) = Space              // back to SPACE
   ENDWHILE
   Name ← LEFT(Name, LENGTH(Name) - 1)           // remove the space
   Name ← Name & Dots
   RETURN Name
ENDFUNCTION

criteria.point: Loop to the length of the parameter, or loop until the first non-space character in Line
Extracts a character from Line within a loop (e.g. MID(Line, Count, 1))
Identifies the first non-space character in a loop
Attempt at removing the leading spaces from Line
Leading spaces actually removed / a new string created without the leading spaces
Returns a string following a reasonable attempt at removing leading spaces

rejects: Approach in the scheme: find the position of the first non-space character, then take a substring. Other valid approaches (e.g. WHILE loop stripping the first character while it is a space) can earn the points.
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION DeleteSpaces(Line : STRING) RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE NewLine : STRING
   DECLARE EndOfLeading : BOOLEAN
   DECLARE Count, NumSpaces : INTEGER
   DECLARE NextChar : CHAR
   CONSTANT Space = " "
   NumSpaces ← 0
   EndOfLeading ← FALSE
   FOR Count ← 1 TO LENGTH(Line)
      NextChar ← MID(Line, Count, 1)
      IF NextChar <> Space AND EndOfLeading = FALSE THEN
         NumSpaces ← Count - 1   // the number to trim
         EndOfLeading ← TRUE
      ENDIF
   NEXT Count
   NewLine ← RIGHT(Line, LENGTH(Line) - NumSpaces)
   RETURN NewLine
ENDFUNCTION

Opens both files in the correct modes (input for READ, existing output file for APPEND/WRITE as appropriate) and closes them afterwards

PROCEDURE Stage_2(F1, F2 : STRING)
   DECLARE Line : STRING
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER
   Count ← 0
   OPEN F1 FOR READ
   OPEN F2 FOR APPEND
   WHILE NOT EOF(F1)
      READFILE F1, Line
      Line ← DeleteSpaces(Line)
      Line ← DeleteComment(Line)
      IF Line <> "" THEN
         WRITEFILE F2, Line   // skip blank lines
      ELSE
         Count ← Count + 1
      ENDIF
   ENDWHILE
   CLOSEFILE F1
   CLOSEFILE F2
   OUTPUT Count, " blank lines were removed"
ENDPROCEDURE

PROCEDURE TwoParts()
   DECLARE NextNum, Average : REAL

   TotalA <- 0.0
   TotalB <- 0.0

   REPEAT
      INPUT NextNum
      TotalA <- TotalA + NextNum
   UNTIL NextNum = 0

   REPEAT
      INPUT NextNum
      TotalB <- TotalB + NextNum
   UNTIL NextNum = 0

   Average <- (TotalA + TotalB) / 2
   OUTPUT "The average is ", Average
ENDPROCEDURE

FUNCTION Header(Line : STRING) RETURNS STRING

   IF LENGTH(Line) >= 13 THEN
      IF TO_UPPER(LEFT(Line, 9)) = "FUNCTION " THEN
         RETURN "F" & RIGHT(Line, LENGTH(Line) - 9)
      ENDIF

      IF TO_UPPER(LEFT(Line, 10)) = "PROCEDURE " THEN
         RETURN "P" & RIGHT(Line, LENGTH(Line) - 10)
      ENDIF
   ENDIF

   RETURN ""

ENDFUNCTION

items.context_note: Teacher's program analyses pseudocode projects; Header(Line) classifies a line as a procedure header, function header or neither, and FindModules(FileName) fills the global 2D string array ModInfo (column 1 line number, column 2 "P"/"F", column 3 module description).

criteria.point: Opens the file in READ mode and subsequently closes it

items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE FindModules(FileName : STRING)
   DECLARE Line : STRING
   DECLARE Index, LineNum : INTEGER

   OPENFILE FileName FOR READ

   Index <- 1
   LineNum <- 0

   WHILE NOT EOF(FileName)
      READFILE FileName, Line
      LineNum <- LineNum + 1
      Line <- Header(Line)
      IF Line <> "" THEN
         ModInfo[Index, 1] <- NUM_TO_STR(LineNum)
         ModInfo[Index, 2] <- LEFT(Line, 1)
         ModInfo[Index, 3] <- RIGHT(Line, LENGTH(Line) - 1)
         Index <- Index + 1
      ENDIF
   ENDWHILE

   CLOSEFILE FileName

ENDPROCEDURE

FUNCTION GetDate(ProductionDate : DATE, ShelfLife : INTEGER) RETURNS DATE
   DECLARE NewDate : DATE

ENDFUNCTION

Loop executes the correct number of times
Concatenates an asterisk to the start/end of the masked string inside the loop
Assigns / keeps the last four characters of the card number (e.g. RIGHT(CardNumber, 4))
Returns the masked string
NON-LOOP ALTERNATIVE: takes the right number of asterisks from a constant string of 20 asterisks (e.g. LEFT(Asterisks, Count)) after calculating how many

FUNCTION Conceal(CardNumber : STRING) RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE MaskedString : STRING
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER
   CONSTANT Asterisk = '*'

   MaskedString ← RIGHT(CardNumber, 4)
   FOR Count ← 1 TO LENGTH(CardNumber) - 4
      MaskedString ← Asterisk & MaskedString
   NEXT Count

   RETURN MaskedString
ENDFUNCTION

   DECLARE MaskedString : STRING
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER
   CONSTANT Asterisks = "********************" // 20 asterisks

   MaskedString ← LEFT(Asterisks, Count) & RIGHT(CardNumber, 4)

Write pseudocode for the function AdjustClock(). Use the date functions from the insert: `SETDATE(Day, Month, Year : INTEGER) RETURNS DATE` and `DAYINDEX(ThisDate : DATE) RETURNS INTEGER` (Sunday = 1, Monday = 2, ...), among others.

criteria.point: Function heading with INTEGER parameter, ENDFUNCTION and RETURNS INTEGER
Declares a local INTEGER variable used to create a date / hold a day number
Loop until the 3rd Sunday is found (loop solution)
Attempts to use both SETDATE() and DAYINDEX()
Correctly generates a DATE with SETDATE() for the day in March (in the loop, or for 1st March in the non-loop solution)
Tests whether the date is a Sunday using DAYINDEX() = 1 (non-loop: calculates third Sunday for a value returned by DAYINDEX for one day)

items.max_note: max 7 (eight marking points listed for either solution)
rejects: Two solution styles are accepted: loop solution (increment the day from 1 until three Sundays have been counted) and non-loop solution (SETDATE for 1 March, DAYINDEX, then calculate the third Sunday for every possible day index).
For the non-loop style, the third Sunday is 15 if 1 March is a Sunday, otherwise 23 - DAYINDEX(1 March).
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION AdjustClock(ThisYear : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE ThisDayNumber, SundayCount : INTEGER
   DECLARE ThisDate : DATE
   ThisDayNumber <- 0
   SundayCount <- 0
   REPEAT
      ThisDayNumber <- ThisDayNumber + 1
      ThisDate <- SETDATE(ThisDayNumber, 3, ThisYear)
      IF DAYINDEX(ThisDate) = 1 THEN
         SundayCount <- SundayCount + 1
      ENDIF
   UNTIL SundayCount = 3
   RETURN ThisDayNumber
ENDFUNCTION

Conditional outer loop correctly formed, with a Boolean flag declared and initialised

items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE Sort()
   DECLARE Temp, J, Boundary : INTEGER
   DECLARE NoSwaps : BOOLEAN

   Boundary <- 1999

   REPEAT
      NoSwaps <- TRUE
      FOR J <- 1 TO Boundary
         IF Reading[J, 1] > Reading[J+1, 1] THEN
            //first swap sensor value
            Temp <- Reading[J, 1]
            Reading[J, 1] <- Reading[J+1, 1]
            Reading[J+1, 1] <- Temp
            //now swap corresponding ID
            Temp <- Reading[J, 2]
            Reading[J, 2] <- Reading[J+1, 2]
            Reading[J+1, 2] <- Temp
            NoSwaps <- FALSE
         ENDIF
      NEXT J
      Boundary <- Boundary - 1
   UNTIL NoSwaps = TRUE
ENDPROCEDURE

A coffee shop loyalty scheme stores for each customer a customer ID (a unique six-digit string) and points (an integer that rises by one for each cup of coffee ordered).

When a customer orders coffee:
- the total points increase by the number of coffees ordered;
- if one cup is ordered and the points go above 10, that cup is free and points are reduced by 11;
- if several cups are ordered and points go above 10, they get one free coffee for every 11 points, and points are reduced by 11 for each free coffee.

Example: a customer has 9 points and orders 16 cups: points become 25, they get 2 free coffees and have 3 points left.

Module CustomerOrder() is called with two integer parameters (the number of coffees ordered, and the current number of points). It outputs a suitable message giving the number of free coffees and returns the new points total.

Write pseudocode for module CustomerOrder().

criteria.point: Function header and ending, with both integer parameters and an INTEGER return type
Number of coffees ordered is added to the points
Correct calculation of one free coffee (points of 11 or more give a free coffee and reduce the points by 11)

Outputs the number of free coffees with a suitable message
Returns the new points total

rejects: Mark scheme MP4 says 'attempted calculation' of multiple free coffees, so a loop or DIV/MOD attempt can gain the mark even if not fully correct.
Mark scheme model solution also caps free coffees at the number ordered (Number > 0).
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION CustomerOrder(Number, Points : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER

   DECLARE NewPoints, NumberFree : INTEGER

   NewPoints <- Points + Number
   NumberFree <- 0
   WHILE NewPoints >= 11 AND Number > 0
      NumberFree <- NumberFree + 1
      NewPoints <- NewPoints - 11
      Number <- Number - 1
   ENDWHILE

   OUTPUT "Number of free coffees is: ", NumberFree
   RETURN NewPoints
ENDFUNCTION

PROCEDURE AddNewCustomers(NumToAdd : INTEGER)

   DECLARE CustomerID : INTEGER
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER
   DECLARE Line : STRING
   DECLARE NewLine : STRING
   OPENFILE "Loyalty.txt" FOR READ

   WHILE NOT EOF("Loyalty.txt")
      READFILE "Loyalty.txt", Line
   ENDWHILE
   CLOSEFILE "Loyalty.txt"

   OPENFILE "Loyalty.txt" FOR APPEND

   CustomerID <- STR_TO_NUM(LEFT(Line, 6))

   FOR Count <- 1 TO NumToAdd
      CustomerID <- CustomerID + 1
      OUTPUT CustomerID
      NewLine <- NUM_TO_STR(CustomerID) & ",0"
      WRITEFILE "Loyalty.txt", NewLine
   NEXT Count

   CLOSEFILE "Loyalty.txt"
ENDPROCEDURE

FOR loop; 4. loop for elements 1 to 1000 / 0 to 999; 5. check if current element contains the required ID, in a loop; 6. if found correctly return loyalty points // store the correct points and return after the loop; 7. check if current element is 99999 and return -1 / break the loop, in a loop; 8. return -1 if ID not found. BINARY SEARCH ALTERNATIVE points: 1. header/ending with correct parameter and return type; 2. range check, return -1 if outside; 3. conditional loop that halves the search space each iteration; 4. check if CustomerID is stored in the current array element, in the loop; 5. mechanism to end the loop if found, in the loop; 6. mechanism to end the loop if not in the array, in the loop; 7. if found return the correct loyalty points; 8. if not in the array return -1. Model: Start <- 1; End <- 1000; WHILE Start <= End; Mid <- (Start + End) DIV 2; IF Loyalty[Mid, 1] = CustomerID THEN RETURN Loyalty[Mid, 2]; ELSE IF Loyalty[Mid, 1] > CustomerID THEN End <- Mid - 1; ELSE Start <- Mid + 1; ENDIF; ENDWHILE; RETURN -1.
Mark points 4 and 7 (conditional-loop scheme) and points 5, 7 (FOR-loop scheme) are marked 'in a loop'.
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION FindCustomer(CustomerID : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER
   DECLARE Found : BOOLEAN
   CONSTANT Unused = 99999
   CONSTANT Upper = 1000
   Found <- FALSE
   Index <- 1
   IF CustomerID < 10001 OR CustomerID > 11000 THEN
      RETURN -1   // Out of range value for customer ID
   ENDIF
   WHILE Found = FALSE AND Loyalty[Index, 1] <> 99999
      IF Loyalty[Index, 1] = CustomerID THEN
         Found <- TRUE
      ELSE
         Index <- Index + 1
      ENDIF
      IF Index > Upper THEN
         RETURN -1
      ENDIF
   ENDWHILE
   IF Found THEN
      RETURN Loyalty[Index, 2]
   ELSE
      RETURN -1
   ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION

PROCEDURE PointsReport()
   DECLARE Count : INTEGER

   DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
   DECLARE Average : REAL

FUNCTION RollDice(NoOfTimes : INTEGER) RETURNS REAL

items.prompt:
A module Parity() takes a string parameter BitString representing a binary value (it only contains the characters '0' and '1'). It adds one character to the end of BitString: '0' if BitString contains an even number of 1s, or '1' if it contains an odd number of 1s. The modified BitString is returned.

Examples: "0010010110" returns "00100101100" (even number of 1s so '0' appended); "101010" returns "1010101" (odd number of 1s so '1' appended).

Write pseudocode for the module Parity().

criteria.point: Function heading and ending, with a STRING parameter and STRING return type
Loop that runs for the length of BitString
Extracts the current character inside the loop
Compares the current character with '1' (or '0') inside the loop
Increments a count, which was initialised earlier, inside the loop
Checks whether the number of 1s is even or odd (e.g. Count MOD 2)
Appends '1' or '0' as appropriate
Returns the amended BitString

items.final_answer:
FUNCTION Parity(BitString : STRING) RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE Index, Count : INTEGER
   Count <- 0

   FOR Index <- 1 TO LENGTH(BitString)
      IF MID(BitString, Index, 1) = '1' THEN
         Count <- Count + 1
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index

   IF Count MOD 2 = 1 THEN
      BitString <- BitString & '1'
   ELSE
      BitString <- BitString & '0'
   ENDIF

   RETURN BitString
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION Generate(Number : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Total, Index, CheckDigit : INTEGER
   DECLARE NumString : STRING

   Total <- 0
   NumString <- NUM_TO_STR(Number)

   FOR Index <- 1 TO LENGTH(NumString)
      Total <- Total + STR_TO_NUM(MID(NumString, Index, 1))
   NEXT Index

   CheckDigit <- Total MOD 10

   Number <- Number * 10 + CheckDigit
   RETURN Number
ENDFUNCTION

// Alternative (no conversion to string):
FUNCTION Generate(Number : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
   DECLARE Total, CheckDigit, Remainder, Num : INTEGER
   Num <- Number
   Total <- 0
   WHILE Num > 0
      Remainder <- Num MOD 10
      Num <- Num DIV 10
      Total <- Total + Remainder
   ENDWHILE
   CheckDigit <- Total MOD 10
   Number <- Number * 10 + CheckDigit
   RETURN Number
ENDFUNCTION

PROCEDURE OKToBorrow(ThisStudentID : STRING)

FUNCTION ReturnBook(ThisStudentID, ThisBookID : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN

Write pseudocode for a function `Compare()` that compares two strings. It has four parameters: two strings `String1` and `String2`; a character `Position` which is 's' (compare String1 with the START of String2) or 'e' (compare String1 with the END of String2); and a Boolean `CaseMatters` (TRUE = upper and lower case letters such as 'A' and 'a' are different, FALSE = they are treated as the same). It returns FALSE if String2 has fewer characters than String1; otherwise it returns TRUE if the comparison is true and FALSE if not.

Examples:

| String1 | String2 | CaseMatters | Position | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| "Cat" | "Catalogue" | TRUE | 's' | TRUE |
| "CAT" | "Catalogue" | TRUE | 's' | FALSE |
| "CAT" | "Catalogue" | FALSE | 's' | TRUE |
| "Cat" | "Catalogue" | TRUE | 'e' | FALSE |
| "GUE" | "Catalogue" | FALSE | 'e' | TRUE |
| "Catalogue" | "Cat" | TRUE | 's' | FALSE |

(The insert lists LEFT, RIGHT, LENGTH, TO_UPPER and other functions you may use.)

criteria.point: Correct function heading with all four parameters (String1, String2 as STRING; CaseMatters as BOOLEAN; Position as CHAR), RETURNS BOOLEAN, and ENDFUNCTION
Calculate the length of String1 (e.g. LENGTH(String1))
If String2 is shorter than String1 return FALSE
Compare the (modified) strings, String1 against the relevant part of String2
Test CaseMatters; if FALSE, convert both strings to the same case (TO_UPPER or TO_LOWER)
Test Position for 's' / 'e' and form the modified string(s): LEFT(String2, length of String1) for 's', RIGHT(String2, length of String1) for 'e'
Return the appropriate BOOLEAN value in all cases

rejects: MP5 needs the CaseMatters test AND the conversion of both strings to the same case.
MP6 needs the test for 's'/'e' AND forming the modified string(s) in one or both cases.
Mark scheme: the function heading mark needs parameters, ending and return type together.
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION Compare(String1, String2 : STRING, CaseMatters : BOOLEAN, Position : CHAR) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE S1Length : INTEGER

   S1Length <- LENGTH(String1)
   IF LENGTH(String2) < S1Length THEN
      RETURN FALSE // String2 is shorter than String1
   ENDIF

   IF CaseMatters = FALSE THEN
      String1 <- TO_UPPER(String1)
      String2 <- TO_UPPER(String2)
   ENDIF

   CASE Position
      'e' : String2 <- RIGHT(String2, S1Length)
      's' : String2 <- LEFT(String2, S1Length)
   ENDCASE

   IF String1 = String2 THEN
      RETURN TRUE
   ELSE
      RETURN FALSE
   ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION

PROCEDURE CountLoans(ThisStudentID : STRING)

FUNCTION NewLoan(ThisStudentID, ThisBookID : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER
   DECLARE IsStored : BOOLEAN
   CONSTANT Blank = ""

   Index <- 1
   IsStored <- FALSE

   WHILE Index <= 7000 AND NOT IsStored
      IF Loan[Index].StudentID = Blank THEN
         Loan[Index].StudentID <- ThisStudentID
         Loan[Index].BookID <- ThisBookID
         Loan[Index].OnLoan <- TRUE
         IsStored <- TRUE
      ENDIF
      Index <- Index + 1
   ENDWHILE

   RETURN IsStored
ENDFUNCTION

   IF Loan[Index].StudentID = Blank THEN
      Loan[Index].StudentID <- ThisStudentID
      Loan[Index].BookID <- ThisBookID
      Loan[Index].OnLoan <- TRUE
      RETURN TRUE
   ENDIF
NEXT
RETURN FALSE

items.prompt:
In the check digit method (sum of the digits of the original number, remainder when divided by 10 is the check digit, appended as the last digit), the new number is input and the check digit is used to validate it. The original number is always at least three digits.

A function CheckNumber() takes an integer value and returns TRUE if the check digit is correct, otherwise FALSE.

Write pseudocode for CheckNumber(). Assume the parameter is valid.
items.context_note: Check digit = (sum of digits of the original number) MOD 10, appended to the end of the original number.

criteria.point: Function header with correct identifier, parameter and return type (RETURNS BOOLEAN)
String route: use NUM_TO_STR to convert the parameter // (excluding the last digit) // Numeric route: initialise the running sum before the loop
Extract the check digit: last character of the string (RIGHT(...,1)) converted to a number // Number MOD 10 (the least significant digit of the parameter)
Loop for LENGTH of the string - 1 following correct conversion // Numeric route: loop WHILE Number > 0
Attempt to form the sum of the digits in a loop (string route: MID/STR_TO_NUM; numeric route: MOD and DIV)
Completely correct sum of the digits (excluding the check digit) in a loop, with the sum initialised before the loop
Calculate the check digit from the sum: Total MOD 10
Compare the calculated check digit with the final digit of the parameter and return the appropriate Boolean value

items.max_note: 8 points listed, max 7. Two accepted routes with their own marking points (string route above; numeric route below).
rejects: Numeric route marking points: header; initialise Sum; set CheckDigit to the least significant digit of Number (Number MOD 10); loop while Number > 0; attempt to use MOD and DIV to sum successive digits in the loop; completely correct sum of all digits apart from the least significant; calculate check digit from the sum; compare with CheckDigit and return the Boolean.

Numeric route example: Remainder <- Number MOD 10; Number <- Number DIV 10; CheckDigit <- Remainder; Sum <- 0; WHILE Number > 0: Remainder <- Number MOD 10; Number <- Number DIV 10; Sum <- Sum + Remainder; ENDWHILE; IF Sum MOD 10 <> CheckDigit THEN RETURN FALSE ENDIF; RETURN TRUE.
Loop upper bound alternative accepted: 1 TO LENGTH(NUM_TO_STR(Number DIV 10)).
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION CheckNumber(Number : INTEGER) RETURNS BOOLEAN
   DECLARE Total, Index, CheckDigit : INTEGER
   DECLARE NumString : STRING

   Total <- 0
   NumString <- NUM_TO_STR(Number)
   CheckDigit <- STR_TO_NUM(RIGHT(NumString, 1))
   // alternative: CheckDigit <- Number MOD 10

   FOR Index <- 1 TO LENGTH(NumString) - 1
      Total <- Total + STR_TO_NUM(MID(NumString, Index, 1))
   NEXT Index

   IF Total MOD 10 <> CheckDigit THEN
      RETURN FALSE
   ENDIF

   RETURN TRUE
ENDFUNCTION

PROCEDURE LoanStatus(ThisStudentID, ThisBookID : STRING)
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER

DECLARE ThisPacket : STRING

DECLARE ThisMachine : CHAR

A programmer has a global 1D INTEGER array Numbers holding 1000 integers (lower bound 1), each initialised to a random integer from 200 to 99 999. A bubble sort sorts Numbers into ascending order. All variables are correctly declared.

algorithm B:
```
Boundary <- 999
REPEAT                                 //Outer Loop
   NoSwaps <- TRUE
   FOR Index <- 1 TO Boundary          //Inner Loop
      IF Numbers[Index] > Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
         //Start of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
         Temp <- Numbers[Index]
         Numbers[Index] <- Numbers[Index + 1]
         Numbers[Index + 1] <- Temp
         //End of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
         NoSwaps <- FALSE
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index
   Boundary <- Boundary - 1
UNTIL NoSwaps = TRUE
```

Explain why algorithm B is more efficient than algorithm A (shown below). Your answer must refer to both the inner and outer loops.

algorithm A:
```
FOR LoopCounter <- 1 TO 999            //Outer Loop
   FOR Index <- 1 TO 999               //Inner Loop
      IF Numbers[Index] > Numbers[Index + 1] THEN
         //Start of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
         Temp <- Numbers[Index]
         Numbers[Index] <- Numbers[Index + 1]
         Numbers[Index + 1] <- Temp
         //End of block to swap neighbouring elements in the array
      ENDIF
   NEXT Index
NEXT LoopCounter
```

criteria.point: MP1 (inner loop): the inner loop iterates one fewer time (in B) each time the outer/repeat loop iterates (Boundary decreases)
MP2 (inner loop): because after each pass of the outer loop one more (the last) element of Numbers is in its correct place
MP3 (outer loop): the outer/repeat loop stops iterating if no swaps are made / all numbers are sorted (NoSwaps stays TRUE)
MP4 (outer loop): so fewer iterations are needed (if the array is not initially sorted)

The outer loop in B stops as soon as a whole pass makes no swaps (the array is sorted), whereas A always runs all 999 passes, so B needs fewer iterations when the array is not initially sorted.

A program encrypts a message using the Caesar Box Cipher idea. Plain text must be 25 characters or fewer; if shorter, spaces are added to the end to make it exactly 25 characters (padded plain text). Example: plain text 'This is a message' (17 characters) becomes padded plain text 'This is a message' followed by 8 spaces.

Write pseudocode for module AddPadding(). It must: prompt for and input the plain text; check it contains between 1 and 25 characters inclusive; re-input until it does; add spaces to the end if needed so that it is exactly 25 characters; return the amended plain text. (It has no parameters and returns a STRING.)
items.context_note: Caesar Box Cipher program; plain text up to 25 characters padded with spaces.

criteria.point: Function heading, RETURNS STRING return type and ENDFUNCTION
Prompt for and input of the plain text
A conditional loop that checks one of the boundary values (1 or 25)
A conditional loop (REPEAT/WHILE) that correctly checks both boundaries (length >= 1 AND length <= 25)
Re-input of the plain text inside the loop
A loop that iterates for the number of spaces to add to the end (e.g. FOR Index <- LengthOfPlaintext + 1 TO 25) - OR, in scheme two, a string of at least 24 spaces to append from
Spaces appended to the plain text (or to an empty string) - OR, in scheme two, correct use of LEFT()/MID() and & to append padding characters
The correctly padded plain text is returned (RETURN) after a reasonable attempt at the padding

items.max_note: one mark per numbered point (8); two mark schemes (loop padding, or LEFT/MID padding)
rejects: MP4 must be a conditional loop; if no loop is used then the boundary-check and re-input points (3, 4, 5) cannot be given.
Alternative padding: WHILE LENGTH(Plaintext) <> 25 ... Plaintext <- Plaintext & Space ... ENDWHILE, or building a SpaceString in a loop and appending it, are accepted by the scheme.
Do not accept use of language-specific string manipulation which is not compatible with the syllabus pseudocode.
In scheme two the mark points are numbered 1-6 with two merged lines (points 3 and 5 each have two parts), giving 8 marks in total.
items.final_answer:
FUNCTION AddPadding() RETURNS STRING
   CONSTANT Space = ' '
   DECLARE Plaintext : STRING
   DECLARE LenOfPlaintext : INTEGER
   DECLARE Index : INTEGER
   REPEAT
      OUTPUT "Enter plaintext"
      INPUT Plaintext
      LenOfPlaintext <- LENGTH(Plaintext)
   UNTIL LenOfPlaintext >= 1 AND LenOfPlaintext <= 25
   FOR Index <- LenOfPlaintext + 1 TO 25
      Plaintext <- Plaintext & Space
   NEXT Index
   RETURN Plaintext
ENDFUNCTION

Scheme two alternative (no loop to pad): CONSTANT Fill = "<24 spaces>" ... Plaintext <- LEFT(Plaintext & Fill, 25) then RETURN Plaintext.

criteria.point: A counter/Index generated from 1 to 25 (or equivalent calculation) used to extract all characters of the plain text
Both Row and Column generated in a loop (e.g. nested FOR loops 1 TO 5)

Identify/isolate all 5 characters for all 5 rows
Output all five rows of Grid, each on a separate line

items.max_note: one mark per numbered point (8); max 7 if the procedure heading/parameter type is incorrect
rejects: Max 7 marks if the procedure heading or parameter type is incorrect.

items.final_answer:
PROCEDURE PopulateGrid(Plaintext : STRING)
   DECLARE Row, Column, Index : INTEGER
   Index <- 1
   FOR Row <- 1 TO 5
      FOR Column <- 1 TO 5
         Grid[Row, Column] <- MID(Plaintext, Index, 1)
         Index <- Index + 1
      NEXT Column
   NEXT Row
   FOR Row <- 1 TO 5
      OUTPUT Grid[Row, 1], Grid[Row, 2], Grid[Row, 3], Grid[Row, 4], Grid[Row, 5]
   NEXT Row
ENDPROCEDURE

            OUTPUT "Bin " & NUM_TO_STR(BinNo)
            BinCount <- BinCount + 1
         ENDIF
      NEXT BinNo
   NEXT Level
   OUTPUT NUM_TO_STR(BinCount) & " bins are not in use"
ENDPROCEDURE

rejects: Do not accept comma syntax when forming the text string (use & concatenation, not commas).
Any loop type is accepted for the level and bin loops (e.g. FOR or REPEAT); loops must cover 3 levels and 120 (or 5) bins.

items.final_answer:
```
FUNCTION FindBin(MySize : STRING) RETURNS STRING
   DECLARE Level, BinNo : INTEGER
   DECLARE Text : STRING
   Text <- "No bins available"
   Level <- 0
   REPEAT
      BinNo <- 1
      REPEAT
         IF Bins[Level, BinNo].Size = MySize AND Bins[Level, BinNo].Active = FALSE THEN
            Text <- "Level: " & NUM_TO_STR(Level) & " Bin: " & NUM_TO_STR(BinNo)
            OUTPUT Text
            RETURN Text
         ELSE
            BinNo <- BinNo + 1
         ENDIF
      UNTIL BinNo = 121
      Level <- Level + 1
   UNTIL Level = 3
   OUTPUT Text
   RETURN Text
ENDFUNCTION
```
